intro: Picture taking the lift up to the 31st floor and stepping out to an infinity pool whose edge seems to spill into the horizon over Pattaya Bay — The Base Pattaya Sea View Residence is a condo in Sansiri's The Base Central Pattaya project, and that image is exactly why a lot of people pick it · it's a 31-storey tower with 1,112 units total, completed around 2016, rented out daily by individual unit owners through OTAs · the star is the rooftop infinity pool with 180-degree sea and city views, plus a sky garden, gym and yoga room · the location is central, on Pattaya Sai 2 Rd, about 150m from Jomtien Beach and around a 10-minute walk to Pattaya Beach · every unit has a kitchenette and balcony, from around THB 1,400/night · but there are a couple of important things to know about the "sea view" that doesn't match the photos in some rooms, and the condo rules you'll want to read before booking

body.html: Who The Base Pattaya Sea View is for, in a nutshell — first, it helps to be clear that The Base Pattaya Sea View Residence isn't a hotel in the traditional sense. It's a large Sansiri condominium where individual unit owners rent their rooms out by the night through online booking platforms · the project itself is called The Base Central Pattaya, a 31-storey tower with around 1,112 units, completed around April 2016, sitting in central Pattaya on Pattaya Sai 2 Rd in the Nong Prue area · because it's a condo, what you get differs from a hotel in that rooms have a kitchenette, fridge, microwave and a private balcony, which suits people who want to cook for themselves sometimes, stay several nights, or mix work with travel · from real reviews and the information we gathered, the people who suit this place best are couples, small families, remote workers, and travellers who want more space than a hotel room at the same price, plus a rooftop pool with sea views · the ones who may not suit it are people expecting full hotel service — a 24-hour front desk, bellhops, and daily housekeeping — because with this kind of condo stay you're mostly looking after yourself · the trade-off you get in return is space, privacy, and better value when you stay several nights — but it also comes with uncertainty about room quality and strict condo rules, which we'll walk through honestly in the next sections

Location and getting around — this is the point reviews agree on most on the praise side · The Base sits in central Pattaya on Pattaya Sai 2 Rd, on the southern stretch that continues toward Jomtien · what a lot of people love is that it's only about 150m from Jomtien Beach, and around a 10-minute walk gets you to Pattaya Beach, so heading down for a stroll by the sea in the morning or evening is easy · within walking distance the area is packed with convenience stores, Thai and international restaurants, massage shops, grocery stores and a night market, so you can handle daily life without relying much on a car · big malls like CentralFestival Pattaya Beach and Terminal 21 Pattaya are about a 5–10 min drive away, and Walking Street about 10–15 min by car · for longer trips, U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is about a 40–50 min drive, and from Bangkok it's around a 2-hour drive · one thing to note about the location is that this stretch of Pattaya Sai 2 is lively and gets congested during rush hour, with bars and nightlife not far away, so if you call a Grab in the evening you may need to allow extra time · driving yourself is easier since the condo has parking, but there's a fee of around 100 baht/day, and during busy periods the parking can fill up

"Great location, just a few steps down to Jomtien Beach. In the evening we went up to the 31st-floor pool and saw the whole bay of Pattaya with the city lights — genuinely beautiful for photos · the room had a kitchenette so we could make our own coffee, good value for the price."

Room types and decor — because The Base is a condo with many different owners renting out, the thing to understand from the start is that the decor and condition of the rooms won't be the same across the board; it depends on how much each owner has invested in furnishing and maintaining their unit · generally the units split into Standard / Superior studios of around 30 sqm that combine the sleeping and living areas, Deluxe sea-view rooms of a similar size but facing the sea, and 2-bedroom units of around 50–55 sqm for families or groups of friends · what all units share is a kitchenette with a stove, fridge, microwave and basic cookware, a private balcony, air conditioning, a TV and an en-suite bathroom · reviews on the positive side say well-kept rooms are clean, nicely decorated, and the view from the balcony is lovely, especially high-floor rooms that genuinely face the sea · but the side that needs a clear warning is the issue of the term "sea view" not matching the photos in some rooms — many reviews complain that they booked a sea-view room but ended up looking only at the wall of the building next door, or blocked by trees and other buildings · on top of that, some reviews say the room was smaller than expected, the balcony was narrow, and units that owners didn't maintain well had old furniture or inconsistent cleanliness · so the key tip is to read the reviews of that specific unit or host carefully before you book, and ask the owner for photos of the actual view before confirming, rather than just looking at the project's overall photos

Facilities, the pool, and the sky garden — the highlight that gets The Base talked about is the rooftop infinity pool (31st floor), whose edge runs out to meet the horizon, with a roughly 180-degree view of Pattaya Bay and the city skyline · reviews say sunset in the evening and after dark when the city lights come on are the moments most people love most — going up to soak and take in the view makes for a nice atmosphere for photos · besides the rooftop pool there's also a quieter ground-floor pool, a kids' pool, several sky garden spots, a well-equipped gym, a yoga room, a playroom for kids, and a basketball court · backed up by key-card security on every floor, digital door locks, CCTV and 24-hour guards · Wi-Fi in the common areas · but to be honest, the rooftop pool comes with very strict rules — many reviews mention that food and drinks (except plain water) aren't allowed up at the pool area, with warnings about fines if you break the rule · another point is that, being a large condo, the common facilities are shared with actual residents and a lot of daily guests, so at peak times there can be a lot of people using them at once and long waits for the lift

Food and dining — The Base doesn't have a hotel-style breakfast service, because it's a condo · but that's actually a plus for many people, since every room has a kitchenette so you can cook for yourself · within walking distance there are dozens of Thai and international restaurants, convenience stores open 24 hours, and supermarkets in nearby malls, so buying ingredients to cook yourself or grabbing food to eat back in the room is easy · reviews from long-stay guests praise how having a kitchen saves a lot on food costs, especially for breakfast and simple meals · for those who want to eat out, the Pattaya Sai 2 and Jomtien area has plenty of options, from budget street-food stalls and beachside seafood restaurants to chill spots by the sea · the thing many reviews warn about is that you can't bring food and drinks up to eat by the rooftop pool under the condo rules, so if you want to sip a drink while enjoying the view you'll have to do it in your room or on the balcony instead · overall, dining at The Base is about flexibility — you can choose to cook, take away, or head out, which suits a stay where you use the condo as a base to explore the city and the beaches

Service and check-in — this is the point that differs most from a hotel, and it's something to understand before booking · because The Base is rented out by individual owners or small agents, check-in usually means arranging to collect the key from that room's representative, not a central hotel desk · reviews on the good side say many owners look after guests well, reply to messages quickly, are easy to meet for the key handover, and give tips on what to do in Pattaya · but the side that needs a frank warning has several parts · one, some reviews say check-in times are limited (around 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM) and there's an extra fee if you arrive outside those hours · two, some guests have complained about overly strict damage charges even for minor marks on the furniture · three, the condo's security is fairly strict, and under the law, daily rentals shorter than 30 days in a condo without a hotel licence are against the rules, so some reviews mention guards or the building's management checking on daily guests · to be safe, choose a host with plenty of reviews and a good reputation, confirm the check-in details, key handover time, and damage-charge terms clearly before you travel, and keep proof of your booking

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly clear and quite "two-sided" · On the praise side: a central Pattaya location near Jomtien Beach and walkable to Pattaya Beach, the 31st-floor infinity pool with gorgeous sea and city views especially in the evening, rooms with a kitchen and balcony giving good space for the price, well-maintained rooms that are clean and nicely decorated, and good value when you stay several nights · On the watch-out side: the most talked-about issue is the "sea view" that doesn't match the photos in some rooms — you book one but end up seeing a building wall or being blocked · next is noise, because it's near a bar district and a busy street; some reviews say flat out that it was "as loud as sleeping next to a bar" · then there are the strict condo rules and damage charges, rooms smaller than expected, inconsistent room quality because each unit's owner maintains it differently, and long lift waits at peak times, plus a few harsher reviews mentioning cleanliness problems like insects in some rooms · most of these gripes can be managed by picking a unit with good reviews, asking for photos of the real view, and setting your expectations correctly — that you're staying in a condo, not a hotel

"The rooftop pool and the view are the real deal, gorgeous at sunset · but the room we booked said sea view and we could only see a sliver of sea because the building next door blocked it, and on Friday night the noise from below carried up to the room. Next time I'll ask the owner for photos of the actual view before booking."

Price and value — daily rental at The Base starts at around THB 1,400/night for a Standard/Superior studio on weekday low-season dates, rising to roughly THB 1,900–2,800+ for a sea-view room or on weekends and in high season · 2-bedroom units of 50–55 sqm run from around THB 2,800 and up depending on size and view · compared with daily-rental condos in the same area like Centric Sea Pattaya, which is similarly priced, The Base feels good value for its location near the sea and the 31st-floor rooftop pool view that's hard to find at this price · but that value comes with having to look after yourself more, taking on the risk of room quality that isn't guaranteed, and the uncertainty of a view that may not match the photos · if you're planning to stay several nights, cook for yourself sometimes, pick a unit with good reviews and confirm the view with the owner first, the money you spend is well returned · but if you're only staying a night or two and want easy, no-surprises service, a central chain hotel may be a more reassuring choice

What to know before booking — there are several things that help make a stay at The Base go more smoothly · one, choose a host with plenty of reviews and a good score, and read that unit's reviews in detail rather than just the project overview, because the quality of each room varies a lot · two, if the sea view matters to you, ask the owner for photos of the actual view from that room's balcony before confirming, because the "sea view" in some rooms may be blocked by a building or trees · three, confirm the check-in time, key pickup point, and the terms for out-of-hours fees and damage charges clearly before you travel, because some rooms limit check-in times and charge strictly for damage · four, if you're a light sleeper and sensitive to noise, ask for a high-floor room or one on the inner side that doesn't face the street or the bar district · five, be prepared that there's no hotel-style service such as daily housekeeping or a 24-hour desk, and there's a pool rule against bringing food and drinks up · six, go for free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet, and compare prices across several platforms because each unit and channel is priced differently

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, The Base Pattaya Sea View Residence is the best fit for people who want a condo-style room with a kitchen and balcony, plus a 31st-floor rooftop infinity pool with sea views in central Pattaya near Jomtien Beach, on a manageable budget · its location near the sea and walkable to Pattaya Beach, the room space that's larger than a hotel room at the same price, and the rooftop pool view that really is beautiful make it worthwhile, especially for people staying several nights or mixing work with travel · but you have to accept honestly that this is a condo stay, not a hotel — room quality is inconsistent because each owner maintains things differently, the "sea view" in some rooms doesn't match the photos, there's noise from a lively area, the pool rules and damage charges are strict, and check-in means arranging to collect the key yourself · if you pick a unit with good reviews, ask for photos of the real view before booking, confirm the details clearly, and set your expectations right, The Base gives a worthwhile Pattaya stay with a sea view at an accessible price · but if you want easy, no-surprises service and you're only staying a few nights, a central chain hotel may answer your needs more directly

honestSummary: The Base Pattaya Sea View Residence is a Sansiri condo for daily rental that suits people who want a room with a kitchen and balcony, plus a 31st-floor rooftop infinity pool with sea views in central Pattaya near Jomtien Beach, on a manageable budget — a location near the sea, with a genuinely beautiful pool view · but you have to understand it's a condo, not a hotel: room quality is inconsistent, the "sea view" in some rooms doesn't match the photos, there's noise from a lively area, and the condo rules are strict

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — The Base Pattaya Sea View Residence

faq.q: Where is The Base Pattaya Sea View Residence · what's within walking distance?
faq.a: It's on Pattaya Sai 2 Rd in the Nong Prue area, in central Pattaya · about 150m from Jomtien Beach and around a 10-minute walk to Pattaya Beach · about a 5–10 min drive from CentralFestival Pattaya Beach and Terminal 21, around 10–15 min by car to Walking Street, and about 40–50 min to U-Tapao Airport (UTP)

faq.q: Is The Base Pattaya a hotel or a condo?
faq.a: It's a Sansiri condominium (the The Base Central Pattaya project) where individual unit owners rent their rooms out by the night through online booking platforms · every unit has a kitchenette, fridge and balcony · it differs from a hotel in that there's no central 24-hour desk, check-in usually means arranging the key handover with the owner, check-in hours are limited, and the quality of each room varies depending on who looks after it

faq.q: How much does The Base Pattaya start at · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,400/night for a Standard/Superior city-view studio on weekdays · Deluxe sea-view rooms and 2-bedroom units run in the range of around THB 1,900–2,800+ · prices vary by unit and by channel, so compare several platforms and read that unit's reviews before booking

faq.q: Is the sea view at The Base Pattaya a real view?
faq.a: The 31st-floor infinity pool genuinely has beautiful sea and city views · but the "sea view" of some units doesn't match the photos; many reviews complain that they booked a sea-view room but ended up blocked by a building or trees · we recommend asking the owner for photos of the actual view from that room's balcony before confirming, and choosing a high-floor room that genuinely faces the sea

faq.q: What swimming pools and facilities does The Base Pattaya have?
faq.a: It has a 31st-floor rooftop infinity pool with 180-degree sea and city views, a ground-floor pool and a kids' pool · plus a well-equipped gym, sky garden, yoga room, playroom, basketball court, and key-card security with 24-hour guards · there's a rule against bringing food and drinks (except plain water) up to the pool area

faq.q: What should you watch out for when booking The Base Pattaya?
faq.a: Because it's a condo with many owners renting out, you should choose a host with plenty of reviews and a good score, read the unit's reviews in detail, ask for photos of the real view, and confirm the check-in time, key pickup point, out-of-hours fees, and damage-charge terms clearly before you travel · some reviews mention strict damage charges and strict pool rules, so keep proof of your booking and take photos of the room's condition when you check in
